formulas.name: Percentage change
formulas.formula_text: % change = (New value − Old value) ÷ Old value × 100
formulas.assumptions: Old value is non-zero; like-for-like comparison.
formulas.limitations: Base effects distort small bases; not annualised.

formulas.name: Compound annual growth rate
formulas.formula_text: CAGR = (End value ÷ Start value)^(1 ÷ n) − 1
formulas.limitations: Hides volatility within the period.

formulas.name: Contribution
formulas.formula_text: Contribution = Sales − Variable costs
formulas.assumptions: Costs correctly split into fixed and variable.
formulas.limitations: Short-term measure; fixed costs excluded.

formulas.name: Contribution margin ratio
formulas.formula_text: CM ratio = Contribution ÷ Sales × 100
formulas.limitations: Single-product or constant mix assumption for breakeven use.

formulas.name: Breakeven point (units)
formulas.formula_text: Breakeven units = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit

inputs_json.name: contribution_per_unit
inputs_json.description: Selling price minus variable cost per unit

formulas.assumptions: Linear costs and revenues; constant mix; single period.
formulas.limitations: Ignores stepped fixed costs and demand constraints.

formulas.name: Breakeven point (revenue)
formulas.formula_text: Breakeven revenue = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution margin ratio

inputs_json.name: cm_ratio
inputs_json.description: Contribution margin ratio as a decimal

formulas.limitations: As for breakeven units.

formulas.name: Margin of safety
formulas.formula_text: Margin of safety = (Budgeted sales − Breakeven sales) ÷ Budgeted sales × 100

inputs_json.name: breakeven_sales
inputs_json.description: Breakeven sales in the same units

formulas.limitations: As for breakeven; a thin margin signals high operational gearing.

formulas.name: Degree of operating leverage
formulas.formula_text: DOL = Contribution ÷ Operating profit
formulas.assumptions: Fixed costs constant over the relevant range.
formulas.limitations: Point measure — changes with sales level; not in the syllabus knowledge reference.

formulas.name: Current ratio
formulas.formula_text: Current ratio = Current assets ÷ Current liabilities

inputs_json.name: current_assets
inputs_json.description: As per statement of financial position

inputs_json.name: current_liabilities
inputs_json.description: As per statement of financial position

formulas.limitations: Window-dressing; says nothing about asset quality or timing.

formulas.name: Quick ratio (acid test)
formulas.formula_text: Quick ratio = (Current assets − Inventory) ÷ Current liabilities
formulas.assumptions: Receivables are collectible in the short term.
formulas.limitations: Still a snapshot; excludes timing of flows.

formulas.name: Receivable days
formulas.formula_text: Receivable days = Trade receivables ÷ Credit sales × 365
formulas.assumptions: Sales are on credit; year-end balance is typical.
formulas.limitations: Seasonality distorts; use averages where available.

formulas.name: Payable days
formulas.formula_text: Payable days = Trade payables ÷ Credit purchases × 365

inputs_json.name: credit_purchases
inputs_json.description: Annual credit purchases (or cost of sales as proxy)

formulas.limitations: Proxy denominators weaken precision.

formulas.name: Inventory days
formulas.formula_text: Inventory days = Inventory ÷ Cost of sales × 365
formulas.limitations: Obsolete stock overstates the 'days' picture.

formulas.name: Cash conversion cycle
formulas.formula_text: CCC = Inventory days + Receivable days − Payable days
formulas.limitations: Period-end snapshot; seasonal businesses need averages.

formulas.name: Gross profit margin
formulas.formula_text: Gross margin = Gross profit ÷ Revenue × 100
formulas.limitations: Mix changes can move the margin without efficiency change.

formulas.name: Net profit margin
formulas.formula_text: Net margin = Profit after tax ÷ Revenue × 100 (state if operating profit is used instead)
formulas.limitations: Affected by financing and tax, not just operations.

formulas.name: Return on capital employed
formulas.formula_text: ROCE = Operating profit ÷ Capital employed × 100

inputs_json.name: capital_employed
inputs_json.description: Total assets − current liabilities (or equity + non-current debt)

formulas.limitations: Book values; asset age distorts comparisons.

formulas.name: Return on equity
formulas.formula_text: ROE = Profit after tax ÷ Equity × 100
formulas.limitations: Leverage flatters ROE; use with gearing.

formulas.name: Asset turnover
formulas.formula_text: Asset turnover = Revenue ÷ Total assets
formulas.assumptions: Assets stated gross of depreciation effects consistently.
formulas.limitations: Industry asset-intensity differs; compare like with like.

formulas.name: Gearing (debt/equity)
formulas.formula_text: Gearing = Debt ÷ Equity × 100 (state the definition used; alternative: Debt ÷ (Debt + Equity))
formulas.assumptions: Market values preferred; book values if unavailable.
formulas.limitations: Definition varies — always state which is used.

formulas.name: Interest cover
formulas.formula_text: Interest cover = Operating profit ÷ Finance costs
formulas.limitations: Backward-looking; covenants may define it differently.

formulas.name: Present value (single sum)
formulas.formula_text: PV = FV ÷ (1 + r)^n
formulas.assumptions: Rate constant; cash flow timing certain.
formulas.limitations: Result is only as good as the discount rate.

formulas.name: Future value (single sum)
formulas.formula_text: FV = PV × (1 + r)^n
formulas.limitations: Compounding frequency must match the rate.

formulas.name: Present value of an annuity
formulas.assumptions: Payments at each period end; constant rate.
formulas.limitations: Adjust for annuities-due (payments in advance).

formulas.name: Future value of an annuity
formulas.limitations: Not named in the syllabus knowledge reference; supplementary aid.

formulas.name: Net present value
formulas.formula_text: NPV = Σ [CFt ÷ (1 + r)^t] − Initial investment, t = 1..n
formulas.assumptions: Cash flows are incremental and after tax; nominal/real consistency.
formulas.limitations: Sensitive to discount rate and distant forecasts.

formulas.name: Internal rate of return
formulas.formula_text: IRR = r such that Σ [CFt ÷ (1 + r)^t] − Initial investment = 0
formulas.assumptions: Conventional cash flows (one sign change) for a unique IRR.
formulas.limitations: Multiple IRRs possible; reinvestment assumed at IRR; misranks mutually exclusive projects.

formulas.name: Payback period
formulas.formula_text: Payback = Initial investment ÷ Annual cash inflow (even flows); else the time when cumulative inflows first cover the outlay
formulas.limitations: Ignores time value and post-payback flows.

formulas.name: Discounted payback period
formulas.formula_text: Discounted payback = time until cumulative discounted cash flows first cover the initial investment
formulas.limitations: Still ignores post-payback flows; not named in the syllabus knowledge reference.

formulas.name: Weighted average cost of capital
formulas.formula_text: WACC = (E ÷ V) × Ke + (D ÷ V) × Kd × (1 − T)
formulas.assumptions: Constant target capital structure; market-value weights.
formulas.limitations: Single WACC misprices projects of different risk.

formulas.name: Capital Asset Pricing Model
formulas.formula_text: Ke = Rf + β × (Rm − Rf)
formulas.limitations: Single-factor; historical betas are unstable.

formulas.name: After-tax cost of debt
formulas.formula_text: Kd(after tax) = Kd(pre-tax) × (1 − T); approximation for irredeemable debt: annual interest ÷ net proceeds

inputs_json.name: Kd_pre_tax
inputs_json.description: Yield to maturity or effective interest rate

formulas.assumptions: Tax relief is available on interest.
formulas.limitations: Approximation only — beyond the syllabus knowledge reference; use YTM properly where examinable.

formulas.name: Enterprise value bridge
formulas.formula_text: Equity value = Enterprise value − Net debt ± non-operating items; EV = market cap + net debt (+ minorities, − associates)

inputs_json.name: enterprise_value
inputs_json.description: Value of the firm to all capital providers

formulas.limitations: Bridge items (leases, pensions, minorities) often mismeasured.

formulas.name: Sensitivity / switching value
formulas.formula_text: Sensitivity = % change in NPV ÷ % change in variable; switching value = variable value at which NPV = 0

inputs_json.name: variable
inputs_json.description: Key input varied over a plausible range

formulas.assumptions: One variable varied at a time.
formulas.limitations: Ignores correlations between variables.

formulas.name: Expected NPV across scenarios
formulas.formula_text: Expected NPV = Σ (probability of scenario × scenario NPV)
formulas.assumptions: Scenarios are coherent and exhaustive enough; probabilities justifiable.
formulas.limitations: False precision if probabilities are guesses.

formulas.name: Gordon growth (dividend discount) model
formulas.formula_text: P0 = D1 ÷ (Ke − g)

inputs_json.name: g
inputs_json.description: Constant dividend growth rate, g < Ke

formulas.limitations: Very sensitive to (Ke − g); unsuitable for non-dividend payers.

formulas.name: P/E multiple valuation
formulas.formula_text: Equity value = EPS × P/E multiple (of comparable firms)
formulas.assumptions: Comparables are truly comparable; earnings maintainable.
formulas.limitations: Market mood embedded in multiples; growth differences ignored.

formulas.name: Asset-based valuation
formulas.formula_text: Net asset value = Total assets − Total liabilities (± adjustments to market values)
formulas.assumptions: Assets restated to market value where material.
formulas.limitations: Ignores intangibles and going-concern value.

formulas.name: Relevant cost decision rule
formulas.formula_text: Include: future incremental cash flows + opportunity costs. Exclude: sunk costs, committed costs, allocated fixed overheads.
formulas.limitations: Fixed costs become relevant in the long run.

formulas.name: Make-or-buy comparison
formulas.formula_text: Compare: relevant in-house cost (variable + avoidable fixed + opportunity cost) vs supplier price
formulas.limitations: Strategic capability and supply risk are qualitative.

formulas.name: Special order acceptance rule
formulas.formula_text: Accept if: incremental revenue > incremental cost + opportunity cost of capacity used
formulas.assumptions: One-off; no effect on regular prices.
formulas.limitations: Repeated 'special' orders change the analysis; price leakage risk.

formulas.name: Limiting factor ranking
formulas.formula_text: Rank products by: contribution per unit ÷ limiting-factor units per unit; allocate the scarce resource to the highest rank first
formulas.assumptions: Single binding constraint; fixed prices and costs.
formulas.limitations: Multiple constraints need linear programming.

formulas.name: Material variances
formulas.formula_text: Price variance = (Standard price − Actual price) × Actual quantity; Usage variance = (Standard quantity − Actual quantity) × Standard price
formulas.limitations: Variances interact (cheap material → adverse usage).

formulas.name: Labour variances
formulas.formula_text: Rate variance = (Standard rate − Actual rate) × Actual hours; Efficiency variance = (Standard hours − Actual hours) × Standard rate
formulas.limitations: Idle time and learning effects need care.
